sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT] One Filipino seafarer died in an explosion aboard the Marshall Islands-flagged oil products tanker MT Velos Sapphire in the Persian Gulf in the early hours of Nov 5, while the vessel was sailing toward Sitrah, Bahrain; 21 other Filipino crew were unharmed; the tanker was towed to Bahrain's Khalifa Bin Salman Port for investigation; no pollution or environmental damage reported; the seafarer's name is withheld. [UNKNOWN / UNVERIFIED] The cause: DMW says initial reports 'suggested a possible drone attack' but the cause 'remains unverified'; no party has claimed the strike and no attacker is confirmed. [CONTEXT] Seatrade Maritime (Nov 8) counts nine vessels confirmed attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf since Nov 1, including two UKMTO-reported Nov 7 incidents (tanker on fire, crew abandoned 8nm NW of Khasab at 19:20 UTC; second tanker struck by an unknown projectile at 20:20 UTC, crew safe) -- those two map to the IRGC mine-strike claims already recorded Nov 7/8; the 'nine' is Seatrade's own count, not a PortWatch counted figure.
sections.what_verified: The death rests on the DMW's own statement (the primary source). Tiered carrier: AFP (T1) via Manila Times. Philippine outlets (Inquirer, Daily Tribune, Philstar, Malaya, NewsWatch Plus) carry the same DMW statement but have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration. Seatrade Maritime (Nov 8) independently confirms the DMW death report in its own reporting.
sections.what_disputed: DMW itself: cause 'remains unverified'; no claimant; no UKMTO advisory or CENTCOM statement on the Nov 5 incident found in-window. The DMW graphic is a file photo of the ship at sea, not damage imagery.
sections.why_matters: The shipping war's first named human cost: a seafarer killed aboard a tanker in the Gulf while the strait runs at a fraction of normal traffic. Frame as the newly confirmed first seafarer death, not breaking news (event Nov 5, confirmed Nov 7).
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (DMW statement Nov 7; AFP wire via Manila Times Nov 9 00:15 +08:00 = Nov 8 20:15 ; zero 'Velos Sapphire' mentions in any Nov 8 or Nov 9 scan -- grep confirms; missed by all Nov 8 scans) -- Filipino seafarer killed in explosion aboard MT Velos Sapphire in the Persian Gulf, Nov 5; 21 Filipino crew unharmed; cause unverified, initial reports suggested a possible drone attack

totw_analysis: Our read: The shipping war's first named human cost: a seafarer killed aboard a tanker in the Gulf while the strait runs at a fraction of normal traffic. Frame as the newly confirmed first seafarer death, not breaking news (event Nov 5, confirmed Nov 7). The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should Filipino crews keep sailing the Gulf for hazard pay, or should Manila pull them out until the shipping war ends? (DMW Facebook comments: grief plus anger at DMW/shipowners sending crews through Hormuz; 'paldo' hazard-pay debate.)
